title: Why do you watch movies? What do they mean to you?

commenti.body: [removed]

Honestly, I see all of those things as essentially the same thing. They're not separate to me. Movies are stories, and great stories inspire, motivate, and move us; they can help us empathize and understand new perspectives, or reinforce our own. Great stories also get us interested in what makes them work and enraptures us with their artistry, and great stories are escapism by nature of being a story at all and not being my own life. I watch movies for the same reason that I read novels and play video games, I like being moved and losing myself in the lives and experiences of characters. Regardless of what kind of story it is, it's something new and different from my own milquetoast life, even if it's just someone else's milquetoast life. There's really no feeling quite like being moved by a story, and movies are just one of many art forms to do that. The ability of a director to control the pace and visuals so precisely give them their sense of immersion, and that can be powerful.
Simple escapism. Nothing more complicated than that.
Film is an aesthetic and heightened distillation of experience laden with meaningful emotion and structured with purpose. A very enjoyable *poem* in the Greek sense — a created object.
I always have hope that a movie will offer an entire new perspective about life and will improve our change the way I see the world. Or at least to offer some incredible experience to watch.

Why be stuck experiencing one reality when you can view infinite realities. 

I travel a lot and love it, but even still I can never travel to Finland during WW2 (Sisu), France during the Revolution (Chevalier), or fight vampires in New Orleans (Renfield). But I got to experience a taste of all those things with movies I saw this past week

Movies can fit any mood.

I like to watch action movies and superhero movies for fun and excitement. Horror and psychological thrillers can also fit these descriptions. 

I love bio pics like Ray and The Doors for the story. Movies based on books also have great stories like Stephen King.

Then there are also movies that I appreciate as works of art. Bergman, tarkovsky, Lynch, Malick, Kubrick. Just beauty and poetry in motion.

There is much to offer and much to love in movies, which is why they are so popular.

It’s an escape from reality. With film, you can escape reality and put yourself into any sort of world you want. You can be in a fantasy world, a superhero world, a mystery world, anything. Reality has no limits in film, cuz you are creating your own reality in your own image
I've been watching movies & shows since childhood. The moving pictures combined with sound and music have always captivated me. It's a quite human feeling I believe.

Depends

If I'm watching a James Cameron film, those movies are fun in the same way an amusement park is fun

If I'm watching Kubrick, I'm probably watching to appreciate film as an artform 

But usually, I'm watching because I find the story and/or vibes interesting. 

I think most entertainment could be considered a form of escapism and film can transport you to different worlds probably more effectively than any other type of art

*"Movies are the most powerful empathy machine in all the arts. When I go to a great movie I can live somebody else's life for a while. I can walk in somebody else's shoes. I can see what it feels like to be a member of a different gender, a different race, a different economic class, to live in a different time, to have a different belief."* \- Roger Ebert
I started watching American movies when I was 8 so I can learn English. I also found them entertaining.
Good answer.

I'm paraphrasing but I always loved what Joseph Gordon Levitt said about movies once in an interview..."they help me understand the world. They're a reflection of the world...etc." This has always resonated with me. I think movies make you a better person, in understanding other walks of life, empathizing. The less pretentious answer would be, I love to be thrilled and I love to be taken on a ride. Top Gun: Maverick is a perfect example of this.
Escapism
To experience all kinds of different emotions and maybe have something new to think about afterwards.

That is a great way to put!  I saw the film numerous times during its initial theatrical release... and when it would reappear at midnight showings.  And I've watched it perhaps another 30+ times over the years and I never drew that connection... but you nailed it!
>*"Don't you understand, Steven? Somebody has to kill the babysitter."*

>I want to strap on some weapons and help my team survive a zombie apocalypse (Dawn of the Dead-1978)

What I love most about *Dawn of the Dead* isn't the vicious satire. It's the fun adventure underneath, grown adults playing Fort with real guns.
Escape from this dickturd planet. Too much depressive shit out there. All these visual stories make it easier to endure. Now and then you also learn something.
To be entertained.

Teacher, mother, secret lover. -Homer J. Simpson.
I know he meant t.v., but it works for this, too.
Dive into another worlds and be entertained
For me it is either stories, entertainment and art.
Escapism and I like to see how the creators of movies view their fellow humans.

Q: Why do you watch movies?

A: **Escapism.**  I want to take 1.5-2 hours to explore something new and different than real life.  As a Christian within a social group of other Christians, I'm an oddball because I avoid those heart-tugging, tear-jerking films about life's struggles.  

I don't need to watch a movie about reality... I just need to look in the mirror... and open the front door.

I want to join the crew of the Proteus and explore the human body (**Fantastic Voyage**\-1966).  

I want to explore the depths of the earth with Sir Lindenbrook **(Journey to the Center of the Earth**\-1959).  

I want to work with the team building a spaceship before the Earth is destroyed (**When Worlds Collide**\-1951)

I want to strap on some weapons and help my team survive a zombie apocalypse (**Dawn of the Dead**\-1978)

I want to explore the Moon in a Victorian-era spacecraft (**First Men in the Moon**\-1964)

You get the idea. :D

I love the cinema. Being at the movie theater is how I feel many people who are devout in their faith feel at their place of worship. I no longer feel the pressures of the world on me, I no longer think of any bad times. I’m just there to enjoy a story. I also love the filmmaking process and seeing shots like the oner in The Protector or the top down dragon breath scene in John Wick 4 gives me huge serotonin hits in my brain as I try to figure out how they managed to do it.
To appreciate reality more, I'm such a daydreamer that I forget how beautiful reality is. I love movies that remind me about an aspect of everyday life.
Because they make me emotional.
I love visual story telling. I really enjoy seeing the techniques good film makers employ to be able to tell a story without using tons of exposition dialogue
They mean a great deal. A necessary occasional escape to maintain my sanity
depends on the mood i am in
A form of escape. We can living vicariously through them. Imagining and experiencing impossible scenarios, while in reality we struggle to pay off a one bedroom apartment with an unfulfilling career.

For me it's art and i admire art it's a medium through which different cultures and different customs more clearly different people etc can be explored. For me it's a passage way to another world which is different or similar to mine but which offers another perspective

I love stories. It allows me to be immersed in their world if only for a little bit of my time. 

It's interesting to see different takes on the same story/characters. Like this week, I watched Peter Pan 1953, Peter Pan 2003, and Pan 2015. I can't believe I didn't watch the 2003 version sooner. It's easily my favorite out of those 3.

I like stories.

Same reason I read books, comics, mangas, manhwas, watch TV shows or play video games.
